newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Labour union asks ban on China funds for HK groups.
newsitem.headline: Labour union asks ban on China funds for HK groups.

text.p: A powerful pro-Beijing labour union in Hong Kong has made an unusual call for a ban on funding from China's ruling Communist Party to local political groups in the territory, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The Federation of Trade Unions said the ban should be added to planned curbs on political rights in the British colony after it reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, the South China Morning Post reported.
Curbs planned by future Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa would bar funding from overseas, and it was only fair that money from the Chinese mainland also be stopped, the federation said.
"This will avoid disputes and criticisms. Hong Kong's political groups should stand on their own feet to fight for their beliefs," it quoted union boss Cheng Yiu-tong as saying.
The 210,000-member pro-China federation also called for a clearer definition of political groups to be covered by Tung's controversial proposals.
The unions' remarks were the latest in a flood of feedback in a "consultation" process ending on Wednesday that was intended to gauge public opinion on the proposals.
Federation officials were not immediately available to comment.

Human rights activists and lawyers have slammed Tung's plans to boost controls on organisations involved in politics and on public protests after Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule, saying the proposals are misguided and unnecessary.
Under Tung's proposals, launched earlier this month, groups involved in politics would be banned from receiving funds from abroad, but donations from the Chinese mainland would be unaffected.

China's National People's Congress, or parliament, has declared parts of Hong Kong's Public Order and Societies ordinances incompatible with its Basic Law, Beijing's mini-constitution for the territory after the handover.
Tung's future secretary of justice, Elsie Leung, has expressed willingness to consider calls for a ban on mainland funding to be included.
Such funding had not originally been mentioned because it was considered that the national security interests of Hong Kong and mainland organisations were the same, Leung said on Monday.
"But we will consider this proposal as so many people have raised it," she said.
